Here’s why those 500s are happening and how to fix them quickly.

### Why POST /api/orders returns 500
- Root cause: Schema mismatch in Appwrite “orders” collection vs what `OrdersService.createOrder()` writes.
  - Service writes fields like `user_id`, `title`, `description`, `price`, `status`, `comments`, `total_pages`, `total_sections`, `wizardData`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, etc.
  - Your existing collection likely has old fields like `userId`, `orderNumber`, `totalAmount`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or is missing the new ones entirely.
  - Appwrite rejects unknown/missing attributes; the error gets wrapped and you see “Http Exception” 500.

What to do (server-side)
1) Align collection attributes with the service
- Ensure the “orders” collection has at least:
  - Strings: `user_id` (req), `title` (<=255), `description` (<=4000), `payment_status` (default 'pending'), `comments` (<=1000), `wizardData` (>=16384), `payment_gateway` (<=50), `callback_url` (<=500), `return_url` (<=500)
  - Numbers: `price` (float), `total_pages` (int), `total_sections` (int)
  - Datetime: `created_at`, `updated_at`
  - Strings: `status` (e.g., 'pending'|'in_progress'|'completed'|'cancelled')
- If you previously used `userId`, add `user_id` and keep `userId` only until you backfill and fully migrate.

2) Make create idempotent/secure and set owner permissions
- In `OrdersService.createOrder(...)`, pass document permissions:
```ts
import { Permission, Role } from 'node-appwrite';

// ...
await databases.createDocument(
  databaseId,
  ordersCollection,
  ID.unique(),
  { ...data }, // the same payload you have now
  [Permission.read(Role.user(userId)), Permission.write(Role.user(userId))]
);
```

3) Improve error visibility temporarily (so 500s show real cause)
- Wrap `createDocument` in try/catch and log `error.message` (and `error.response` if present) before re-throwing an HttpException.

4) Run your schema update
- If you need a quick stopgap for `wizardData` and `payment_status` run: `node update-orders-schema-simple.js`
- Then add the missing attributes listed in step 1 (either extend `update-orders-schema.js` or create a small add-attributes script) and deploy.

No frontend change needed for /orders payload. Keep sending what you’re sending; the backend owns `user_id`.

### Why POST /api/messaging/topics returns 500
- Root cause: You repeatedly create the same topic ID (deterministic from name), Appwrite returns 409 “already exists”, and the controller throws a generic Error → 500.
- Also ensure “subscribe” values are valid roles like `user:<USER_ID>` (yours look correct).

What to do (server-side)
- Make topic creation idempotent and return 200/201:
```ts
async createTopic(topicId: string, name: string, subscribe: string[]) {
  try {
    return await this.messaging.createTopic(topicId, name, subscribe);
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err?.code === 409) {
      // treat as success; optionally fetch and return the topic if API supports it
      return { $id: topicId, name, subscribe };
    }
    throw new Error(`Failed to create topic: ${err.message}`);
  }
}
```
- Or in the controller, catch 409 and return a success response instead of throwing.

Frontend workaround (optional)
- If the topic is per-user, call the endpoint once on first login and ignore “already exists” responses, or gate on a local flag.

- If you still get 500 on /orders after schema alignment, the logged Appwrite message will pinpoint the exact missing attribute or type.
